title: MobiFriends: 3.5M accounts breached
summary: In January 2020, the Barcelona-based dating app MobiFriends suffered a data breach that exposed 3.5 million unique email addresses. The data also included usernames, genders, dates of birth and MD5 password hashes.

title: Moneycontrol: 762.9K accounts breached
summary: In April 2021, hackers posted data for sale originating from the online Indian financial platform, Moneycontrol. title: Yam: 13.3M accounts breached
summary: In June 2013, the Taiwanese website Yam.com suffered a data breach which was shared to a popular hacking forum in 2021. The data included 13 million unique email addresses alongside names, usernames, phone numbers, physical addresses, dates of birth and unsalted MD5 password hashes.

title: Livpure: 269.6K accounts breached
summary: In August 2020, the Indian retailer Livpure suffered a data breach which exposed over 1 million customer purchases with 270 thousand unique email addresses. The data also included names, phone numbers, physical addresses and details of purchased items.

title: Daily Quiz: 8M accounts breached
summary: In January 2021, the quiz website Daily Quiz suffered a data breach that exposed over 8 million unique email addresses. The data also included usernames, IP addresses and passwords stored in plain text.

title: IIMJobs: 4.2M accounts breached
summary: In December 2018, the Indian job portal IIMJobs suffered a data breach that exposed 4.1 million unique email addresses. title: WedMeGood: 1.3M accounts breached
summary: In January 2021, the Indian wedding planning platform WedMeGood suffered a data breach that exposed 1.3 million customers. The breach exposed 41.5GB of data including email and physical addresses, names, genders, phone numbers and password hashes. The data was provided to HIBP by dehashed.com.

title: DriveSure: 3.7M accounts breached
summary: In December 2020, the car dealership service provider DriveSure suffered a data breach. The incident resulted in 26GB of data being downloaded and later shared on a hacking forum. Impacted personal information included 3.6 million unique email addresses, names, phone numbers and physical addresses.
